subsystems.name: Collector elements
subsystems.role: intercept sunlight and convert it to usable energy; individually very thin and light so that huge areas become feasible.

subsystems.name: In-space mining and refining
subsystems.role: supplies the material a swarm needs without launching it all from Earth.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing and assembly
subsystems.role: builds new collectors, then builds copies of the factories themselves.

subsystems.name: Autonomous control
subsystems.role: manages millions of independent units and their orbital spacing without real-time human input.

subsystems.name: Power transmission
subsystems.role: sends the collected energy to where it is wanted, or relays it between units.

subsystems.name: Ground reception
subsystems.role: converts a received beam back into grid electricity.

buildSteps.title: Prove beamed power at useful scale
buildSteps.detail: A demonstration satellite collects sunlight, converts it to microwaves or laser light, and delivers a measured amount of power to a rectenna on the ground. This has been demonstrated only at small pilot scale.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate off-Earth materials
buildSteps.detail: Robotic missions extract water, metals and silicon from asteroid or lunar material and refine them into usable feedstock. Only sample-return-scale work exists today.

buildSteps.title: Build a pilot factory in space
buildSteps.detail: A small plant takes that feedstock and produces simple structures — booms, films, panels — using mostly solar heat and electricity rather than Earth-supplied parts.

buildSteps.title: Close the replication loop
buildSteps.detail: The plant is upgraded so that its own components — deposition heads, motors, control boards — can be made from local material, initially with a high imported fraction, then with less.

buildSteps.title: Position collectors in near-Sun orbit
buildSteps.detail: Collectors are placed at roughly 0.4 astronomical units, where sunlight is several times more intense than near Earth, and spaced so they neither shadow nor collide with one another.

buildSteps.title: Beam and receive
buildSteps.detail: Energy is transmitted by microwave or laser to a receiving station; because a beam spreads with distance, transmitter and receiver apertures must be very large to keep losses acceptable across interplanetary distances.

buildSteps.title: Scale by replication
buildSteps.detail: Each generation of factories builds more factories, giving exponential growth in collector area — the mechanism that makes a swarm conceivable at all.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise the swarm
buildSteps.detail: Long-term control keeps orbital elements from drifting, manages heat rejection in vacuum, and prevents debris from cascading through the fleet.

prerequisites.why: reusable rockets have cut launch cost sharply, but a swarm must be built mostly from material already in space.
the mass required is planetary in scale, so shipping it from Earth is implausible.
exponential growth is the only route to a structure this large within a human timescale.
microwave and laser power transmission works over short ranges; interplanetary distances demand enormous apertures and high pointing accuracy.
millions of moving collectors need collision avoidance that no human team can supervise.

pathway.milestone: orbital demonstrations of solar power beaming and robotic satellite servicing
pathway.unlocks: evidence that collecting and transmitting power in space works at all.

pathway.milestone: asteroid and lunar resource extraction feeding an in-space manufacturing pilot
pathway.unlocks: structures built off Earth instead of launched from it.

pathway.milestone: a self-expanding factory that measurably grows its own output
pathway.unlocks: exponential rather than linear growth in collector area.

pathway.milestone: a partial swarm in near-Sun orbit delivering a significant share of a civilisation's energy
pathway.unlocks: a route toward full stellar-scale energy capture, if the materials and control problems can be solved.
